headline: Every tray of chicken checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to your processing site
heroLede: At around 900,000 birds a week, a lifted seal or the wrong cut on a label is hard to catch by eye. Here's what a camera check could look like on your tray line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every tray has its film on, sealed all the way round, with no chicken caught in the seal. A leaking tray of raw chicken is the kind of fault that comes back as a retailer complaint.
labelLede: Breast fillets and thigh fillets look much the same through the film. The camera checks every tray carries the right label for the cut, straight and intact, so the shopper gets what the label says.
codeLede: Fresh chicken has a short shelf life, so the use-by date has to be right on every tray. The system reads the printed date and batch code and compares them with the product and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Glove pieces, blue plastic and tray offcuts are all close at hand in a processing plant. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a crate.
